intro: Living alone near WashU (Washington University in St. Louis) doesn't require a luxury-tower budget. There are Studios clustered in Skinker-DeBaliviere, the Delmar Loop, and a few in Central West End for the medical campus students.
Every listing below is live right now, with the walk time to campus already worked out and reviews from students who lived in the building. No landlord fluff, no stale listings from last year.
directAnswer: Studio apartments near WashU sit mostly in Skinker-DeBaliviere and near the Delmar Loop, with some in the Central West End. Every rent on this page is live, and newer buildings near the Loop cost more than older walk-ups a few blocks back.

faqs.q: How much does a studio near WashU cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the block and the building. Newer buildings near the Loop run higher, and older walk-ups usually cost less. The live rent is on each listing above.

faqs.q: Is a studio cheaper than splitting a bigger apartment?
faqs.a: Usually not. Sharing a 2 or 3 bedroom typically puts your share below what a studio costs, because you're splitting the unit price. A studio is what you pay for having zero housemates. If budget matters more than privacy, check the 2 and 3 bedroom pages.

faqs.q: When should I start looking for a studio?
faqs.a: Early. Studios are the smallest slice of inventory near WashU, and students report private landlords start signing for the next school year as early as November. WashU affiliated companies like Quadrangle open later, usually in spring. If you see a studio you like in the fall, don't sit on it.

faqs.q: Do studios near WashU come furnished?
faqs.a: Rarely. Furnished units are scarce across this market and studios are no exception. Filter for furnished on the browse page. If you strike out, budget a few hundred dollars for basics or look at a sublease, which often comes with the furniture already there.

benchmarkNote: Rents on this page are each listing's current asking rent. Proximity does not publish averages computed from its own listings.
